title: Compound interest as a geometric sequence
problem: $\$8000$ is invested at $4\%$ per annum compound interest. Find the value after 6 years (to the nearest cent), and find how many complete years it takes to exceed $\$10\,000$.

steps.instruction: Identify the geometric model for the balance after $n$ years.
steps.working: Each year, the balance is multiplied by $1.04$. So the balance after $n$ years is: $$A_n = 8000 \times (1.04)^n$$ This is a geometric sequence with $a = 8000 \times 1.04$ and $r = 1.04$.

steps.instruction: Find when the balance first exceeds $\$10\,000$.
steps.working: Solve $8000 \times (1.04)^n > 10000$: $$(1.04)^n > 1.25$$ $$n \ln(1.04) > \ln(1.25)$$ $$n > \frac{\ln 1.25}{\ln 1.04} = \frac{0.22314}{0.03922} \approx 5.69$$ The investment first exceeds $\$10\,000$ after $n = 6$ complete years.

answer: After 6 years the investment is worth $\$10\,122.55$, and it first exceeds $\$10\,000$ after 6 complete years.

title: Depreciation and recurrence relations
problem: A machine is bought for $\$30\,000$ and loses $18\%$ of its value each year. Set up a recurrence relation for its value $V_n$ after $n$ years, and find after how many complete years its value drops below $\$10\,000$.
answer: The value first drops below $\$10\,000$ after $n = 6$ complete years.

title: Total salary as a geometric series
problem: A graduate starts on a salary of $\$55\,000$ and receives a $3.5\%$ raise each year. Find the total salary paid over the first 6 years, to the nearest dollar.
answer: The total salary paid over the first 6 years is approximately $\$360\,266$.
